claims.text: Retention of toughness in high-entropy alloys is controlled by maintaining a uniform, disordered solid solution and a nanocrystalline grain structure.
Thermally induced localized grain-boundary segregation and precipitation act as a microstructural trigger for embrittlement.
A refractory HEA produced by magnetron sputtering can have a single-phase BCC initial structure.
Magnetron-sputtered W-Ta-V-Cr HEA films can exhibit a predominantly nanocrystalline grain structure.
The elements in the proposed initial HEA state are uniformly distributed.
A temperature near 1023 K is a critical threshold at which atomic mobility permits grain-boundary segregation in certain W-based HEAs.
Annealing below the critical temperature does not promote precipitation.
The relevant structural mediator is the nucleation and growth of Cr-V-rich brittle precipitates at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Elevated annealing temperatures enhance atomic mobility and thereby cause elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary segregation results in the nucleation of brittle precipitates.
The grain-boundary precipitates reduce grain-boundary cohesion.
The grain-boundary precipitates limit crack-tip blunting.
Compromising the homogeneous disordered solid solution at interfaces causes a measurable decrease in toughness.
Above-threshold annealing will reduce Charpy impact energy relative to an as-deposited or low-temperature-annealed baseline.
Above-threshold annealing will reduce fracture toughness relative to the baseline.
Above-threshold annealing will produce a shift toward intergranular fracture features.
The as-deposited or low-temperature-annealed baseline preserves the uniform disordered solid solution and nanocrystalline grains without significant grain-boundary precipitates.
The proposed behavior should hold while the primary BCC phase is retained in refractory systems similar to W-Ta-V-Cr.
The hypothesis may not apply to intentionally multiphase or precipitation-hardened alloys.
The critical annealing temperature and magnitude of toughness loss vary with alloy composition and processing history.
